title: Catch the ball of a wooden cup-and-ball toy in its cup
instruction: Take the wooden cup-and-ball toy out of its stand by the handle, swing the ball up and catch it in the cup, then keep the toy upright with the ball in the cup. Only the toy may touch the ball.
context: Cup-and-ball is a toy most people have played with as children, and a classic robot-learning test of dynamic skill: it needs a rhythmic swing, a string that goes slack and a well-timed catch, none of which quasi-static pick-and-place tests.
setup: Axes: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the left, z up from the floor. Two YAM 6-axis arms with parallel grippers (75 mm maximum opening) on 150 x 150 mm, 0.75 m tall gray pedestals at x = 0, y = +/-0.305 m, facing +x; the left arm stays parked. Flat gray floor. A fixed pine floor stand: a dark 300 x 300 x 20 mm base board centred at x = 0.61 m, y = -0.45 m, a 40 x 40 mm post rising to 0.88 m at x = 0.66 m, y = -0.45 m, and a 24 x 20 mm bracket whose top is level with the post's top, holding a vertical sleeve (27 mm bore, 6 mm wall, 40 mm tall, its floor 0.86 m above the floor, with a 30-degree slot facing -y) whose axis is at x = 0.50 m, y = -0.45 m. Prepare a wooden cup-and-ball toy to the cut list and tolerances in the README, 120 g nominal: a red lacquered cup 88.9 mm outer and 76 mm inner diameter, 50 mm tall with a 10 mm floor; a natural 24 mm turned handle 140.5 mm long below the cup (190.5 mm overall); and a yellow lacquered 31.75 mm wooden ball (11 g) on a 533 mm cotton string (2.4 mm) knotted to the handle's -y side 10 mm under the cup. Start: the toy stands upright in the sleeve, handle end on the sleeve's floor and cup up; the string leaves through the slot and the ball hangs still at full length, its centre 0.44 m above the floor, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured in the toy's frame. The ball is in the cup when its centre is inside the cup's wall (at most 22 mm from the cup's axis, 2 mm tolerance) and between the cup's floor and its rim; upright means the handle within 30 degrees of vertical. 0.25: the handle's end has been lifted 10 mm or more above the sleeve's rim. 0.5: with the toy lifted and upright, the ball's centre has risen above the centre of the cup's rim. 1.0: with the toy lifted and upright, the ball has stayed in the cup for 20 consecutive control steps (1 second). Scores are latched. The trial scores 0 for good if a robot part touches the ball (or, in real trials, the string), the ball visibly contacts the floor, stand or a pedestal, the toy falls below 0.30 m, the toy or ball leaves x -0.4 to 1.2 m, y -1.2 to 0.8 m, z up to 1.6 m, or a fixture moves at least 3 mm.
reset_notes: Stand the toy back in the sleeve, handle down, with the string through the slot, and let the ball hang still before each trial. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: 240 Hz PhysX rigid bodies with 20 Hz control. Wood friction 0.45/0.40, restitution 0.4. The native scorer uses physical ball contact impulses. The cotton cord is a slack-capable, massless 533 mm distance limit with no collision, stiffness or drag; it cannot snag or wrap. Cup and sleeve walls are 20- and 12-sided. The ball has no rolling resistance and may keep moving inside the cup.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 in 600 steps; demo: 1.0 in 309 steps.
